answer.why_different: The generated document uses the IS operation name and URI mapping as the basis for the operation metadata, rather than preserving the generic HTTP GET behavior and resource-selection explanation. D1 and D2 are different values that narrow or replace the official meaning; D3 is an additional operation metadata field.
answer.spec_3gpp: The specification defines getMOIAttributes as retrieving one or multiple resources representing managed object instances, and identifies the GET operation on this URI as retrieving one or multiple resources. It also specifies query parameters for selecting and filtering returned resource properties.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI permits summary and description strings on an operation, and defines operationId as a unique identifier for the operation; operationId is recommended for tooling and naming conventions but is not required.
answer.clearer_why: The official summary accurately states that one or multiple resources are read, while its description explains the GET behavior and the attributes and fields query parameters. The generated text is more implementation-specific and its summary suggests that only MOI attributes are retrieved.

citations.quote: This operation retrieves one or multiple resources representing managed object instances.
MOI .../{className}={id} GET Retrieve one or multiple resources representing managed object instances
operationId | `string` | Unique string used to identify the operation.

differences.reason: The generated summary says “Retrieve MOI attributes,” which narrows and mischaracterizes the operation: the specification says it retrieves one or multiple resources, not merely attributes. This is supported by S2 and S7; the differing summary values are visible in C1 and C2.

The generated description replaces the official explanation of GET resource retrieval and attribute/field selection with only an operation-to-URI mapping, losing behavior information relevant to API readers. The specification explicitly covers GET query parameters and resource retrieval in S1 and S2, while C1 and C2 show the lost explanation.

Adding operationId is valid OpenAPI metadata and gives the operation a stable identifier; the generated value also matches the specification's operation name getMOIAttributes. This is supported by S2 and S8 together with the OpenAPI operationId definition and recommendation in O9.

##### 12.1.3.1.5 Operation deleteMOI

This IS operation deletes one or multiple managed object instances. It
is mapped to the NETCONF \<edit-config\> operation. \<edit-config\> can
delete one or more specific MOIs but only indirectly supports scope or
filtered sets of MOIs that are part of the generic deleteMOI 3GPP
operation specification. \<edit-config\> uses a config block, indicating
the MOI(s) to be deleted.

The Netconf operation attribute on the list representing the
baseObjectInstance should be set to delete or remove.

The default-operation parameter should be set to none.

The IS operation parameters are mapped to SS equivalents according to
table 12.1.3.1.5-1 and table 12.1.3.1.5-2.

equivalents

  --------------------------------- ----------------------- ------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  baseObjectInstance                config                  M       A sequence of embedded XML elements inside the \<config\> element. XML elements for all containing MOIs and their ids(keys) shall be included together wilt the XML elements representing the to be deleted MOI and its key.
  scope                             config                  M       BASE\_ONLY supported as default. Multiple MOIs can be specified in the same operation, emulating other scopes.
  filter                            config                  M       Multiple MOIs can be specified in the same operation, emulating filtering.
